findings.title: Network-AI ClaudeHookBridge deny-pattern bypass permits prompt-hidden payloads
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-109331 says Network-AI versions 5.14.0 before 5.15.2 check ClaudeHookBridge deny patterns only against the first present candidate field. A prompt-injected agent can place dangerous payloads in another field, such as Write content or an MCP script parameter, beside a benign file path or command to evade deny rules and write web shells or execute scripts.
evidence_classification: AI Sec Watch discovery and AI classification
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Network-AI npm package 5.14.0 before 5.15.2; ClaudeHookBridge PreToolUse denyPatterns enforcement.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A model-influenced payload can cross from prompt/tool-argument space into command or file-write authority when the policy hook validates only one candidate field.

upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep the new deny-pattern bypass, affected range, and security-control lesson locally.
Keep only the security implication that approval hooks must validate every model-controllable argument field.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE timing and affected range from NVD API; mitigation wording should be checked against the GitHub advisory during ingest.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare with existing Network-AI approval and filesystem-boundary leaves and create a focused hook-policy boundary if needed.
Recheck GHSA-9p2w-prp8-5722 for patched-version and remediation wording.

findings.title: vLLM audio transcription upload exposes FFmpeg IAMF heap overflow
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-109311 says vLLM before 0.29.0 passes uploaded audio to the PyAV/FFmpeg av.open() fallback with only a file-size check. Authenticated remote users can repeatedly upload malformed IAMF containers to /v1/audio/transcriptions, corrupting the heap and crashing the API process.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: vLLM before 0.29.0; /v1/audio/transcriptions audio upload path and PyAV/FFmpeg fallback parser boundary.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Multimodal inference APIs must treat uploaded media as hostile parser input; availability of the model-serving API can be lost through a malformed audio request.

upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep parser-exposure and model-serving availability security facts locally.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for affected version and endpoint from NVD API; ingest should verify GitHub advisory remediation and release tag details.
follow_up_actions: Check vLLM advisory or release notes for whether 0.29.0 is the published fix.
Consider whether this belongs under model-serving runtime input-validation and multimodal parser exposure.

findings.title: Open WebUI leaks OAuth-mode cookies and exposes disabled model backends
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-109292 says Open WebUI 0.6.27 before 0.11.4 can forward the full browser cookie jar to destination servers on OAuth-mode OpenAI-compatible, OpenAPI tool, or terminal connections, enabling session hijack if the destination captures cookies. CVE-2026-109296 says Open WebUI before 0.11.4 lets authenticated users reach disabled model provider backends by supplying explicit backend indexes on Ollama and OpenAI-compatible listing routes, triggering requests with configured API keys and allowing version or connection enumeration.
evidence_classification: public patch commit references in NVD
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Open WebUI 0.6.27 before 0.11.4 for OAuth-mode cookie disclosure; Open WebUI before 0.11.4 for disabled backend access.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI web UIs often bridge user sessions, model-provider credentials, OpenAPI tools, and terminal connections; cookie forwarding and backend-index authorization flaws can turn model/tool connectivity into account or credential exposure.

upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep identity, session-cookie, API-key, and disabled-backend security facts locally.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE timing, affected range, and core descriptions from NVD API; grouping is local collector judgment because both flaws affect Open WebUI connection authorization and credential/session boundaries.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, split into identity/access and data/privacy leaves if the existing Open WebUI leaves do not cover cookie forwarding and disabled backend reachability.
Recheck GitHub advisories and listed commits for final remediation wording.

findings.title: Agno AgentOS authentication and PythonTools flaws expose remote agent authority
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-108818 says Agno versions up to 2.7.3 and 3.0.6 have a missing-authentication issue in auth.py get_authentication_dependency involving the security_key argument; the exploit is public and the project reportedly had not responded. CVE-2026-108816 says Agno up to 3.0.6 has code injection in PythonTools run_python_code through the code argument, with public exploit material and no project response recorded in the CVE text.
evidence_classification: public GitHub issue and advisory references
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agno 2.7.0 through 2.7.3 and 3.0.0 through 3.0.6 for missing authentication; Agno 3.0.0 through 3.0.6 PythonTools for code injection.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An agent framework that exposes AgentOS or Python tool execution remotely needs explicit authentication and deterministic tool-code boundaries; otherwise model- or user-driven actions can become unauthenticated control or code execution.

upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep authentication and Python tool execution security boundaries locally.
Route general framework adoption/workflow practice upstream; local item is the security-control failure.

findings.confidence_notes: Moderate-to-high confidence for CVE timing and descriptions from NVD; CVE text says the project had not responded, so remediation state needs ingest-time recheck.
follow_up_actions: Check whether Agno has since responded or shipped a fixed version.
Decide during ingest whether to split authentication and Python tool execution into separate focused leaves.

findings.title: mac-shell-mcp command whitelist can be bypassed through shell metacharacters
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-108953 says mac-shell-mcp before 2.0.0 allows MCP clients to bypass the command whitelist by injecting shell metacharacters into execute_command arguments. A malicious prompt or attacker-controlled MCP client can call an allowed command such as pwd with arguments like ';' to run forbidden commands as the server user without approval.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mac-shell-mcp before 2.0.0; execute_command argument handling and command whitelist enforcement.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local shell MCP servers expose high-authority tools to model-influenced clients; whitelist checks must parse and execute arguments without shell injection or approval bypass.

upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep the command-whitelist bypass and local shell authority boundary locally.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for affected range and patch reference from NVD API; ingest should verify the 2.0.0 release state if available.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, connect this to local MCP command execution, approval, and shell-argument parsing controls.

findings.title: Ollama Pull API SSRF has public exploit and 0.34.2 fix
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-108836 says Ollama up to 0.34.1 has SSRF in the Pull API IsValid function in types/model/name.go. The CVE states remote exploitation is possible, exploit details have been publicly disclosed, and upgrading to 0.34.2 with patch dfabde4539e42ba1e1eab50a3a50b88aea7958a0 fixes the issue.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Ollama 0.34.0 and 0.34.1; Pull API model-name validation and server-side fetch boundary.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model pulling is an AI runtime supply-chain and network-fetch path; SSRF can turn model acquisition into unintended internal network access or metadata probing.

upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep Pull API SSRF, affected versions, and model-supply-chain fetch control locally.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE timing, public-exploit status, and fixed version from NVD API; the referenced proof-of-concept repository should be treated as untrusted evidence and not executed.

findings.title: VideoWhisper Site Manager for ChatGPT, Claude, Codex misses authorization
findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-107430 records missing authorization in the WordPress VideoWhisper Site Manager for ChatGPT, Claude, Codex plugin through 1.2.10. The NVD record maps the package as videowhisper-site-manager and records 1.2.11 as unaffected.
evidence_classification: AI Sec Watch discovery and AI classification
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: VideoWhisper Site Manager for ChatGPT, Claude, Codex WordPress plugin through 1.2.10; fixed/unaffected at 1.2.11 per NVD affected-data change entry.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI assistant/admin integrations embedded in WordPress need explicit authorization on management actions; otherwise low-privileged users may reach AI-site management capabilities beyond their role.

findings.title: Repeat-After-Me prompt technique bypasses tool-call authority in six agent frameworks
findings.concise_factual_summary: CSO Online reports that researchers from Pennsylvania State University, Universite Montpellier, and Dartmouth College used a Repeat-After-Me prompt technique to make six agent frameworks execute attacker-controlled tool calls: LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, AutoGen, Google ADK 2.0, AWS Strands Agents, and CrewAI. The same report says their ToFu testing found 253 manually verified bugs across 118 of 273 open-source MCP servers they could run, including path traversal, SSRF, data exfiltration, and OS command injection classes.
evidence_classification: secondary report pending primary paper capture
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Reported framework demonstration includes LangGraph 1.2.0 with Llama 3.1 8B via Ollama; other framework details were reproduced by researchers but not detailed in the article.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The finding separates model refusal from orchestrator authority: syntactically valid tool calls emitted by a model can execute before policy refusal text appears unless the framework independently authorizes each action.

upstream_routing.entity_or_topic: Framework catalogs and broad agent framework context
upstream_routing.local_scope: Keep the security-specific tool-call authorization and MCP bug-class implications locally.
Route broad orchestration/workflow practice upstream; local item is the security evaluation and authority-boundary lesson.

findings.confidence_notes: Moderate confidence because the article is dated and concrete, but the primary paper was not located in this run; details beyond the LangGraph transcript should be treated as secondary until primary evidence is captured.
follow_up_actions: Locate the primary paper or project page before durable synthesis.
